title: docs(skills): correct the dead `cols` layout spelling in SKILL.md
body:
Fixes #5640

`skills/objectui/SKILL.md` is the top-level file of the published skill — the one an agent loads before any guide — and line 81 prescribed the layout key `cols` with `sm` as the base breakpoint. Two files in the same published package already state that this spelling is dead (`rules/protocol.md:252`, `guides/mobile.md:100`), and `AGENTS.md` §5 Commandment 5 states it for the codebase. So the entry file taught the spelling the rule files retire, to a reader who may never open the rule files.

Docs-only. No schema, renderer or registry is touched — the spelling is dead in the code by design; the page was what was wrong.

## Before / after — the only instance changed

`skills/objectui/SKILL.md:81`

```diff
-Layouts are just components that render children. Treat `Grid`, `Stack`, `Container` as first-class citizens. Layout schemas must support responsive props (e.g. `cols: { sm: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 }`).
+Layouts are just components that render children. Treat `Grid`, `Stack`, `Container` as first-class citizens. Layout schemas declare responsive columns on the node as `columns` — a number, or a breakpoint object keyed `xs` / `sm` / `md` / `lg` / `xl`, with `xs` as the base (e.g. `columns: { xs: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 }`).
```

The replacement wording is taken from `rules/protocol.md:235-247` and `AGENTS.md` §5 rather than invented, so the package states one phrasing. `on the node` also carries the envelope half of the same rule, which the old phrase `responsive props` actively worked against.

The prohibition itself was deliberately **not** copied into the entry file. `SKILL.md:126` already links `rules/protocol.md`, where the ❌ lives, and `SKILL.md:140` states that file's own standing discipline — "do not keep a second copy of the answer here".

## Published-skill readings (both required)

| reading | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| changed file, whole file (`skills/objectui/SKILL.md`) | 155 lines | 155 lines | **0** |
| whole package, sum of all `SKILL.md` under the published dir | 155 lines | 155 lines | **0** |
| whole package, all markdown under `skills/` | 5673 lines | 5673 lines | **0** |

Net-line budget zero, as the card and the triage first-touch both required. No sibling gate in this repo defines a token count for skills (`scripts/` carries `check-skills-paths.mjs` and no line/token ratchet), so lines are the measure. Since lines alone would hide the growth, the character reading is reported too and is honest about it: line 81 goes 195 → 319 characters, whole file 8849 → 8973 bytes. That buys the canonical key, the full breakpoint vocabulary and the base — a correction, not an expansion.

## Schema measurement — the substitute evidence

`skills/` is outside `check-doc-snippet-types`' scan surface (#5465 records exactly that), so no gate's green says anything about this sample. It was therefore measured directly, against `GridSchema` and the renderer, **not** against the sibling docs.

Ground truth read from the code:

- `GridSchema`, `packages/types/src/layout.ts:202-209` — declares `columns?: number | Record<string, number>`. No `cols`.
- `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/grid.tsx:57-67` — reads `columns.xs / .sm / .md / .lg / .xl`, with `baseCols = schema.columns.xs ?? 1` and the in-code comment `Note: 'xs' corresponds to base (mobile-first)`.

Measured by rendering both samples through `SchemaRenderer` and reading the emitted class, plus parsing each through the published zod `GridSchema`:

| sample | zod `safeParse` | rendered class |
|---|---|---|
| **after** — `{ type: 'grid', columns: { xs: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 } }` | success, `columns` preserved verbatim | `grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4 gap-4` |
| **before** — `{ type: 'grid', cols: { sm: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 } }` | success, `cols` survives the parse, `columns` gets its default | `grid grid-cols-2 gap-4` |

The after-row matches, class for class, what `guides/mobile.md:99` already claims that schema renders. The before-row is the defect: **a flat two columns at every breakpoint**, which is `rules/protocol.md:252-254` measured rather than quoted.

Base-breakpoint half, measured the same way — this is why `sm` → `xs` is not cosmetic:

| sample | rendered class |
|---|---|
| `columns: { sm: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 }` (the old base key) | `grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4 gap-4` |
| `columns: { xs: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 }` (canonical) | `grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4 gap-4` |

An `sm`-based object never declares its base at all — it lands on the `?? 1` fallback and emits a redundant `sm:grid-cols-1`. That confirms `rules/protocol.md:247` ("`xs` is the base breakpoint; omit it and the base falls back to one column").

### Negative control — reporting the direction actually observed

The dispatch anticipated that the dead spelling would be *rejected* somewhere. Measured, it is **not rejected at any layer** — it is dropped:

| axis | verdict on `cols` |
|---|---|
| TS type (`GridSchema`) | **accepted** — `BaseSchema` carries `[key: string]: any` at `packages/types/src/base.ts:318`, so excess-property checking never fires |
| zod mirror (`GridSchema`) | **accepted** — `safeParse` succeeds and the key survives into `.data` |
| renderer (`grid.tsx`) | silently dropped; `grid-cols-2` at every breakpoint |

The TS leg carries its own control, because "no diagnostic" is otherwise indistinguishable from "the file was never checked": a deliberate `{ type: 'definitely-not-a-grid' }` in the same scratch file **did** report `error TS2322`, proving the file was in the program while the `cols` line drew nothing.

This is the stronger justification for the change, not a weaker one — there is no rejection point anywhere, so an author who reads only the entry file gets a wrong render with nothing thrown and nothing logged. The gap itself is **already on file** and is not re-filed here: #5155 records the `BaseSchema` index signature leaving every component schema open to a misspelled top-level key, and #5250 records the zod passthrough making undeclared keys pass validation. #5157 is the decision-class sibling. Those three remain open and untouched by this PR.

No ablation is available for a docs-only diff, so none was staged.

## Corpus sweep — the whole published package, with a control

Scope: all 29 files under `skills/`, searched with `grep -rnP '(?<!grid-)\bcols\b' skills/`.

Result — three occurrences, one of them the defect:

| hit | disposition |
|---|---|
| `skills/objectui/SKILL.md:81` | **the defect — fixed** |
| `skills/objectui/rules/protocol.md:252` | **left alone** — this is the prohibition, it must keep quoting the dead key |
| `skills/objectui/guides/mobile.md:100` | **left alone** — same, the prohibition |

**Control** (a phrase known to be present, searched the same way, same tool and flags): `grep -rnP '\bcolumns\b' skills/` → 36 hits across 11 files; `grep -rnP 'objectui#4001' skills/` → 2 hits (`rules/protocol.md:254`, `guides/mobile.md:101`). Both returned hits, so a silently-broken search cannot be what produced the short list above.

Widened, same tool: `grep -rnPi '\b(gridCols|columnCount|numCols|colCount|column)\b' skills/` found no further dead spellings, and every `grid-cols-*` occurrence in `skills/` is a Tailwind class name (`rules/styling.md:183,227`, `guides/mobile.md:99,108`, `evals/mobile.json:12`) — correct as written, untouched.

Every breakpoint-object example in the package was also re-read: `rules/protocol.md:242` and `guides/mobile.md:86` already use the `xs` base; `SKILL.md:81` was the only one basing on `sm`.

### The card's eval question, answered

The card asked whether any `evals/*.json` grades the `cols` spelling the way `evals/schema-expressions.json` was found to grade the retired envelope. **It does not.** The only `cols` substring anywhere in `evals/` is `evals/mobile.json:12`, whose `must_contain` entry is the Tailwind class `grid-cols-1` — correct, and unrelated to the schema key. Nothing to change there.

## Verification

Run on the final commit `fc8fa0c1b`, exit codes captured **before** any pipe, each verdict quoted from what the gate itself printed:

| gate | exit | its own verdict line |
|---|---|---|
| `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` | 0 | `Links are valid across 13 scan roots.` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 | `✅  No source of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | 0 | `✅  No changeset declares a \`major\` bump.` |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | 0 | `✅  check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 4916 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |
| `node scripts/check-skills-paths.mjs` | 0 | `✅  check-skills-paths: OK (93/94 stated path(s) resolve across 18 guide file(s); 1 baselined).` |

`check-skills-paths.mjs` is run because this diff edits `skills/**`, which is that gate's entire scan surface.

**No changeset**, on the gate's own instruction quoted above. Verified independently: no `package.json` in the repo declares `skills` in its published `files`, and the root package is private, so nothing under `skills/` ships inside a released npm package. This repo has no `skip-changeset` label mechanism, and none was created.

Control bytes also self-scanned beyond the gate: `grep -naP '[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]' skills/objectui/SKILL.md` → no match.

### Lint narrowing, declared with its three pieces of evidence

A repo-wide `eslint .` was not run. The narrowing is a measurement, not a skip:

1. **Population read from eslint's own config**, not guessed — every `files:` block in `eslint.config.js` targets `**/*.{ts,tsx}` or a narrower TS/TSX subset (lines 28, 159, 179, 201, 215, 245). No block names markdown.
2. **File count read from `--format json`** — `npx eslint skills/objectui/SKILL.md --no-inline-config --format json` exits 0 with one result whose only message is eslint's own verdict: `File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied.` Linted files in this diff: **0**.
3. **Invariance for untouched files** — type-aware linting is not enabled (`eslint.config.js` sets no `projectService`, `parserOptions.project` or `project:`), so no rule reads across file boundaries; and independently this diff changes zero files inside the configured population, so eslint's verdict on every untouched file is identical to `origin/main`'s by construction.

## Not in scope here

`#5465` is not addressed by this PR — it remains open, and is cited above only to explain why the sample had to be measured by hand. `#5155`, `#5250` and `#5157` likewise remain open and untouched; this PR only adds measured corroboration for them in the notes above. `#4001` settled the direction this change follows.
